races.name: EMS Copiers Irish EBF Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Concorde Landed
runners_data.comment: A notable 200,000-euro breeze-up purchase by Sioux Nation, she's out of a dam who excelled over five and six furlongs as a juvenile, with a half-sister useful at a mile, and rates second-highest here at 75. She may just need this experience before showing her best.

runners_data.name: Fly Smartly
runners_data.comment: A costly 135,000-euro daughter of Mehmas, out of a dam smart over seven furlongs at two, rates a strong 73 with us. The yard is out of sorts lately (just one success from 20 runners), so she's perhaps one to note rather than side with on debut.

runners_data.name: My Irish Lady
runners_data.comment: A 160,000-euro filly by Minzaal whose unraced dam is a half-sister to a Graded-placed performer in the US, she's only our second-lowest rated runner here at 62 on debut. The yard is firing on all cylinders currently, which offers her the best chance of outrunning that figure.

runners_data.name: Shi Yang
runners_data.comment: Fifth on her only start, beaten four lengths in a maiden here, this filly races back over the same course, distance and good going just ten days later and rates 74 with us, third best in this field. A wide stall is the obvious concern, but there should be more to come.

runners_data.name: Snowing
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths on her Curragh debut, this filly steps out for a trainer with a strong record at today's track and rates 81 with us, the highest in this field, over suitable trip and ground. A six-week break is the only slight worry.

runners_data.name: Southern Boulevard
runners_data.comment: A 110,000-euro daughter of No Nay Never, out of a dam smart over six furlongs at two and with a half-sister who shone at a mile, rates 73 with us. The stable landed this race last year and clearly respects her chance on debut.

runners_data.name: Woodlawn Lily
runners_data.comment: Sixth then fourth in two starts, including when well held stepped up in grade at this course last time, this speedily-bred filly rates 68 with us. A short break and a yard in good form both work in her favour, but she needs to leave those below-par efforts behind her.

runners_data.name: Arizonaneargalway
runners_data.comment: Sired by Arizona and bought for just 5,000 euros, this filly rates a modest 46 on debut, our outsider here. A dam who was useful over a mile and a half-sister who shone at six furlongs offer encouragement, but she still has plenty to find against this field.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Race

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: A prominent racer for Gary Carroll and G M Lyons, she finished 1st at 5f on good ground last time and brings a strong sim-going record; she is ideally placed to track Keke and challenge late, and her 3-wins-5-places profile at this level makes her the most dangerous rival to the leader.
runners_data.comment: Fairyhouse last time was a stay-related flop over six furlongs, but this gelding won going away before that and drops back to the minimum trip today over conditions that suit. Rated 99 with us, fourth in this quintet, he can bounce back for a trainer in form.

runners_data.name: Keke
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Edward Lynam whose sole confirmed front-running role makes her the race-shaper here; her 12-from-15 sim-going record and a win last time at 6f on good is solid, though her STYLE_FIT flag notes she is racing somewhat out of her most effective role, and W J Lee will need to find the right balance between control and not going too easy.
runners_data.comment: A consistent sort who ran creditably in defeat in a Listed race at Cork last time, this gelding wears a tongue-tie for the first time and rates the pick of this quintet at 101. A strongly run five furlongs on a sound surface should suit down to the ground.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the mount on this hold-up type who has finished second three times in recent starts at 5f on good ground without winning; only six days since last run is worth noting, and in a race where the front pair are likely to control the tempo, a late charge from a true hold-up horse faces an uphill task against a sustainable pace.
runners_data.comment: Below her best when never a threat from off the pace at the Curragh last time, this filly still rates second-highest in this quintet at 100 with us, and her share of places shows she's competitive at this level. A modest strike-rate is the concern, but she's respected on figures.

runners_data.name: Cardiff By The Sea
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for J A Stack whose sole win came on soft ground; her good-ground record reads poorly (0 wins, 1 place from 4 runs), and over five furlongs at Naas, she is unlikely to generate enough late momentum to trouble the principals unless the race is run at an unusually strong pace.
runners_data.comment: A genuine speedster who performed up to expectation when beaten four lengths in a Listed race at Ayr last time, this filly rates 99 with us, third of this quintet, and looks sure to relish a sharply run five furlongs. Faster ground would be the ideal conditions for her.

runners_data.name: Xerling
runners_data.note: An OR-78 three-year-old for Natalia Lupini who won over 5f on good ground and placed again at the same trip; she is a natural closer whose true running style has pushed her into midfield on the map due to the density of hold-up types, and the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution — her chance depends on a pace scenario that this field is not set up to create.
runners_data.comment: This filly won readily by a length and a half in a Cork maiden last time but faces a stiff step up in company here, rating only 85 with us, bottom of this quintet. Versatile on ground and effective at both five and six furlongs, she's up against much higher-rated rivals today.

races.paceDynamic: Keke is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners over five furlongs at Naas on good ground, she is highly likely to dictate at a sustainable tempo without serious pressure from any rival. Howd'yadoit is the only other horse with prominent-racing tendencies, and she will likely track Keke in second, meaning the race is essentially set from the front. Likedbymike, Cardiff By The Sea, and Xerling are all hold-up types who will be posted in behind, relying on a strong finishing kick that a controlled Keke-led pace may not generate for them. This race shape strongly favours Keke and Howd'yadoit — front-end and close-up prominent profiles benefit most when a single horse controls the tempo uncontested, setting a rhythm that suits those on her heels rather than those coming from off the pace. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically be accommodated at the rear, and Xerling — a genuine closer by nature — has been mapped to midfield to reflect the congestion; Keke and Howd'yadoit are most likely to secure the positions that matter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keke Controls, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Keke bowls along in front unchallenged and sets a fair but not scorching tempo, she and Howd'yadoit dictate from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: Keke leads at a sustainable clip with Howd'yadoit shadowing closely, and the pair have first run on the hold-up horses who simply cannot close the gap in time over five furlongs. This shape is the most likely given the lone front-runner status and the inability of the closers to manufacture a strong enough pace to suit themselves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Keke sets enough pace to tie herself up late, Howd'yadoit delivers off her back to nail her close home.
scenarios.body: Howd'yadoit travels smoothly in Keke's slipstream and has enough in reserve to collar her inside the final furlong if Keke overextends even slightly. Gary Carroll's tactical awareness makes this a realistic alternative, as Howd'yadoit has proven capable at 5f on good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Keke sets a genuinely strong gallop that stretches the field early, a hold-up horse generates momentum late.
scenarios.body: Likedbymike has been placed repeatedly at 5f on good ground and could use a fast early pace to motor through from behind; however, a truly strong pace from a single front-runner over just five furlongs at Naas is unlikely to be brutal enough to set the closers up. The reliability of this scenario is limited by the fact that the hold-up horses must rely on conditions they cannot fully control.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops in an unusual or scrambled fashion with no one taking a clear lead or with significant interference, a lower-rated hold-up horse lands a blow.
scenarios.body: Xerling showed a sharp winning performance at 5f on good ground and could theoretically benefit from chaos, but her redistribution from true hold-up to midfield reflects structural disadvantage in this shape. Cardiff By The Sea's sole win came in soft ground and her good-ground record is thin, making this scenario the least credible.

watchPoints.text: Watch Keke's early stride pattern — if W J Lee allows her to coast in front without pressure, the race is effectively decided within the first furlong and a half, with Howd'yadoit the only realistic threat.
Howd'yadoit's draw and early positioning relative to Keke will be critical; Gary Carroll must keep her close enough to have first run without burning petrol chasing a leader who may go easy.

Likedbymike's very short turnaround (6 days) is worth monitoring — if the horse is slightly flat from the quick return, her hold-up style becomes even less effective against a controlled front-running pace.
Cardiff By The Sea's going preference for soft ground means punters should be cautious about her prospects on today's good surface, especially against rivals with stronger good-ground form profiles.

Xerling's redistribution from hold-up to midfield on the map reflects a structural quirk of this field shape — she may race closer than expected if jockey Donagh O'Connor opts for an aggressive early position given the small field.

races.name: Coolmore Stud Blackbeard Tipperary Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Abletai
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Grassick who has placed in both good-ground starts; 56 days since last run is a minor query but going poses no issue, and a clean passage from the rear is essential on a flat 5f track.
runners_data.comment: A close second, beaten only a head in a maiden at this course last time, this colt showed clear progress from debut and rates 87 with us, mid-field of ten. He needs more again stepping up in grade, and has had a lengthy break, but conditions should suit.

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: A.P. O'Brien runner with a win and two placings over course-relevant distances in good ground; races prominently and will be squeezed for position early in a congested 4-horse battle for the prominent berths — getting across cleanly matters.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a Group 2 at Ascot last time over the minimum trip, this colt seemed to want further that day. His overall form, including a recent win, still marks him out as the one to beat here, rating top of this field at 101, with his trainer excelling at this course.

runners_data.name: Hanney Boy
runners_data.note: Consistent placer for McCutcheon who has shown up well in similar ground; naturally prominent but faces stiff competition for that position from more powerful stables, and his OR of 83 suggests he's up against it in Listed company.
runners_data.comment: Third, beaten a length and a quarter, when dropped to five furlongs on good ground at Navan last time, this colt looks capable of more but may need it stepping up in company. He rates 84 with us and is versatile at both five and six furlongs on soft or good.

runners_data.name: Rejoinder
runners_data.note: Listed-rated at OR=120 yet has no form figure logged and no last-run date — a complete unknown for De Aguiar; the style designation is uncertain, and the absence of any public form trail makes him the biggest wildcard in the field.
runners_data.comment: An 82,000-euro breeze-up purchase by Space Blues and half-brother to the high-class Thunder Beauty, a mile performer, this colt rates a bold 89 with us on debut, third in this field of ten. It's admittedly a stiff task first time out, but the pedigree package points to a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.note: Showed only a sixth on debut at Naas in good ground for McLoughlin; lightly raced and rated 120 suggests trainer confidence in unexposed ability, but one run of sixth offers no evidence of a natural racing style or preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight lengths on debut in a maiden at Navan, this filly has speed in her pedigree and should take a step forward for that initial experience, but she rates bottom of this ten-strong field at 74 with us. She looks to have plenty to find against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Belle Island
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for De Aguiar who hasn't run in 76 days; best form has come on standard and standard-to-firm ground rather than good, and the layoff combined with a 5f flat track means she needs everything to fall perfectly from the back.
runners_data.comment: Sent forward too soon and outclassed when comfortably held in a 2yo race at the Curragh last time, this filly needs to recover that form and rates 84 with us, mid-pack in this field of ten. Speedily bred and suited by sound ground, she has been fairly fresh off an eleven-week break.

runners_data.name: Big Negotiator
runners_data.note: The field's sole confirmed front-runner, already a winner over this exact 5f Naas trip in good ground; Twomey sends him here in cracking nick (2/7 T14) and with no rival likely to test him early, W.J. Lee can dictate every fraction — the key horse in any pace analysis.
runners_data.comment: Below her best when beaten seven lengths in the Group 2 Queen Mary at Ascot last time, this filly - fitted with cheekpieces today - had been progressive before that, including a win, and rates 94 with us, second of this ten. She's effective over five and six furlongs on quicker ground, though that Ascot run did expose some limitations up in grade.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Diva
runners_data.note: Won last time out on good ground over 5f and is trained by the small but in-form Dias operation (1/1 T14); races prominently but will need to assert early to avoid the congested pack, and her recent winning form gives her the sharpest recent credentials of the prominent group.
runners_data.comment: Getting off the mark readily by two and a quarter lengths in a maiden at this course last time, this filly steps up in grade today and rates 89 with us, fourth of this ten. She's effective at both five and six furlongs on a sound surface, though there's plenty more required to confirm that improvement at this level.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: Murtagh sends out this OR=120 two-year-old on the back of a recent run 10 days ago; placed on soft but unplaced on good, and her natural running style is unclassified — Ben Coen's tactical awareness will be critical in translating unexposed ability into a result.
runners_data.comment: Beaten ten lengths and never landing a blow from off the pace in a maiden at this course last time, this filly rates 80 with us, ninth of this ten-strong field. Effective over five furlongs on soft ground for a trainer in good form, she's difficult to recommend on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Matriarchal
runners_data.note: Josh Halley-trained filly with a win over this exact course and distance on good ground; races prominently and her Naas form counts directly, though she must navigate the prominent logjam to reproduce that performance.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a novice at Lingfield last time, a below-par effort from this filly who'd won and been placed in the runs before that, she rates 83 with us, well down this field of ten. Effective at five furlongs on soft or all-weather, she faces a stiff task back up in company.

races.paceDynamic: Big Negotiator is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner Listed sprint, and with W.J. Lee aboard a horse already proven over this exact course and trip on good ground, he is expected to stride into a comfortable, uncontested lead from the outset. The prominent group — Carry The Flag, Hanney Boy, Brazilian Diva, and Matriarchal — will jostle for position in the first furlong, creating lateral pressure and potential interference in the 2f-3f zone, though none of them threatens to seriously burn Big Negotiator's early fractions. With a single genuine pace-setter dictating a sustainable, metronomic gallop on a flat course in good ground, the race sets up as a straight-line test of finishing quality rather than a tactical cat-and-mouse, meaning the fractions are unlikely to be either slow enough for a late sprint or fast enough to gut the leaders. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and true closers with a clean run — specifically those capable of producing a sustained, powerful finish in the final furlong once the prominent runners have done their work.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Big Negotiator dictates a smooth, uncontested pace and the prominent runners exhaust themselves fighting for position behind him.
scenarios.body: Big Negotiator strides clear from the break, setting an honest but not suicidal tempo that leaves him with reserves in the final furlong; horses who tracked him prominently at cost find little when the winning post arrives.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion produces a moderate early quarter and the pace proves insufficient to stretch the closers.
scenarios.body: The mid-race scrimmaging among the prominent pack effectively gifts the hold-up types a pace-softened opening two furlongs, and a horse coming with one clean, late run benefits from every stride.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pace War Implodes
scenarios.trigger: If the four contested-prominent runners push the early fractions hard enough to unsettle Big Negotiator and cook themselves.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected opening furlong compresses the field and turns the final 2f into a stamina test, favoring any runner who settled efficiently on the inside rail.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed OR=120 runners with unknown running style shows a precocious turn of foot off a single run or debuts in disguise.
scenarios.body: A horse like Celestial Crown or Rejoinder, having shown enough in limited starts to earn a 120 OR, produces a sharp mid-race move that the field cannot answer.

watchPoints.text: Big Negotiator's early fractions will shape the entire race — if W.J. Lee is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first 2f, the race is effectively set before halfway.

The four-horse battle for prominent positions (Carry The Flag, Hanney Boy, Brazilian Diva, Matriarchal) risks serious interference and bumping between the 3f and 2f marks — any runner inside that group faces a traffic lottery.

Rejoinder carries no form figures and no last-run date — connections have given nothing away, and De Aguiar's other runner Belle Island also has a layoff, suggesting the stable may be operating on limited public evidence.
Abletai's 56-day absence and reliance on a clean run from the rear makes her highly dependent on the prominent horses getting in each other's way — she needs the race to fall apart in front of her.
Good ground is confirmed three times over for the 2:33 slot at Naas, meaning no surface-related excuses — any underperformance will be purely tactical or physical.

races.name: Lawlor's Of Naas Supporting Naas GAA Senior Football Race Day Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Arctic Steps
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with two wins and three places in similar going; Patrick McGettigan takes the ride after 39 days off and headgear flag (p) suggests he needs cover before producing his effort late.|
runners_data.comment: Stepped up in grade and below form when beaten eight lengths off a 74 rating last time, this filly races 2lb lower today and wears cheekpieces for the first time. Admittedly inconsistent, she rates 81 with us, third of this large field, and has previously won from the front over this trip on good or all-weather ground.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran returning after just 6 days, yet his good-ground record across 12 qualifying runs is only 1W2P and he has struggled to make the frame recently — Shay Wallace claims seven.|
runners_data.comment: Form has faded across a run of six of late, though this gelding performed up to that level when beaten five lengths in a handicap at the Curragh last time. He wears a tongue-tie for the first time today, rates 73 with us, mid-field of thirteen, and is best served by yielding or good ground over this trip.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Noel Meade-trained hold-up type who ran 3rd at 5f on good ground last time; back after 27 days wearing blinkers, but a 16th on good ground in the latest comparable run is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Race fitness issues have hampered this gelding, though he carries a fair mark on his best form and lines up from stall thirteen wearing blinkers for the first time. He went too freely too soon at a stamina-sapping track last time, well beaten in a handicap at Navan, but rates 74 with us in this field of thirteen and is suited by five furlongs on good ground.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: Confirmed lead horse who has the pace dynamic squarely in his favour by default, though his STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) is a reminder that he has not always dominated from the front — his stamina at 5f on good ground will be tested if pressed.|
runners_data.comment: Below form when eased off having missed the money in a handicap at Fairyhouse last time, this gelding nonetheless carries a good mark on his all-weather form and had won not long before that. He rates 83 with us, second of this large field, and is effective at five and six furlongs on going from good to yielding.

runners_data.name: Bold Optimist
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse returning from 106 days off; his two wins and three places came largely on standard going and he wears a hood (p) — pressed forward by the crowded rear, he may not reproduce his best.|
runners_data.comment: Performed to expectation when beaten three and a half lengths off a 3lb higher mark at Dundalk last time, this gelding returns from a lengthy break wearing cheekpieces for the first time from a wide draw. He rates 73 with us, mid-field of thirteen, and can defy the layoff to go well again on a sound surface over this trip.

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has placed in 3 of his last 5 on good ground and whose natural hold-up style is squeezed forward by the traffic; E E Ryan (7) is working with a horse that will ideally want to come late but may not get that luxury.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by two lengths off a 6lb lower mark at Down Royal last time, this gelding is up in the weights again today but rates top of this large field at 84 with us. Effective at both five and six furlongs on soft or good ground, he holds obvious claims of building further on that latest success.

runners_data.name: Ardadslosttheplot
runners_data.note: Longest absentee in the field at 277 days, a 3-year-old stepping back to 5f; Rebecca Parsons (7) inherits a horse whose true closing instincts are compromised by the lack of genuine rear space in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Off the track for the best part of a year, this filly was never a factor when beaten five and a half lengths in a nursery at Cork on her latest start. She rates 66 with us, well down this field of thirteen, drawn wide, and needs more to figure back after such a long layoff despite being in good form before that run.

runners_data.name: Cactus
runners_data.note: AP O'Brien's 3-year-old has shown only one top-5 finish from 11 starts on good turf; Freya Frain (7) faces the challenge of finding a passage for a horse that is naturally a closer but cannot realistically settle at the back.|
runners_data.comment: Down the field in a maiden at Cork last time, this filly has been somewhat below par of late but drops back into a handicap today for a trainer who excels at this course. She rates 78 with us, fourth of this large field, and is effective at both five and six furlongs on soft or good ground, though more consistency is needed.

runners_data.name: Jordan Breeze
runners_data.note: Placed in four of last five and won at 5f on soft, Jordan Breeze is one of the more tractable prominent horses here; Robyn Donaghue-Leahy (4) can slot her in just off Sovereign Cry and she is well-suited to this pace shape.|
runners_data.comment: Faded to finish sixth, beaten six and a quarter lengths off a rating of 62 last time, a below-par effort from this gelding who has won and been runner-up twice in recent starts. Racing off the same mark today, he rates 72 with us, mid-field of thirteen, and needs to turn that form around on ground from soft to all-weather over this trip.

runners_data.name: Billboa
runners_data.note: Struggled on good ground historically (1 place from 15 qualifying runs); this six-year-old's natural hold-up profile is hard to execute in a 5f flat sprint — Adam Browne-Souza (7) on a horse with very limited good-ground form.|
runners_data.comment: Stepped up in grade and well beaten in a handicap at Dundalk last time, this gelding is an unknown quantity following his time off and rates near the foot of this large field at 66 with us. He wears a tongue-tie for the first time and is best served by all-weather ground at five or six furlongs.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has won and placed on good ground and ran 2nd at 5f/Good recently; Orla Tynan (7) returns just 3 days after his last run, and while his hold-up style is constrained here, he has the course-going profile to be interesting if gaps open.|
runners_data.comment: Quick to reappear just three days after a below-par effort in a handicap at Fairyhouse, beaten five and a quarter lengths, this gelding rates 72 with us, mid-field of thirteen, and carries a fair mark provided he rediscovers that form. He's fitted with both a tongue-tie and blinkers for the first time and is effective at five or six furlongs on soft or good ground.

runners_data.name: Phil's Dream
runners_data.note: OR 49 makes him the lowest-rated runner; wore tv headgear and was placed at 5f on standard ground, but his good-going figures (2 from 15) are very weak and his redistribution to mid-field only adds to his challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Performed up to par when beaten four and a quarter lengths in a handicap at this course last time, this gelding had been going well before that including a win, and returns fitted with a tongue-tie and visor for the first time. He rates 67 with us, near the foot of this large field, for a yard short of recent success, and needs to find extra to get his head in front off that mark.

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: Highest-rated hold-up horse in the field at OR 73, returning just one day after his last run which is striking; Sadhbh Tormey (7) handles a 3-year-old who wears tb headgear and whose best form at 5f/Good (4th) came on this trip — the quick turnaround is the key query.|
runners_data.comment: Down the field in a handicap at this course last time, this filly looks up against a stiff mark and rates bottom of this field at 64 with us. Fitted today with both a tongue-tie and blinkers for the first time and drawn wide, she's been inconsistent and has plenty to prove, though she is effective over six furlongs on soft or good ground.

races.paceDynamic: Sovereign Cry is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 5f handicap and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, is set to dictate at a sustainable gallop from the gates — a single-pace scenario on good ground over the minimum trip. Jordan Breeze will attempt to sit prominently just off the lead, and while Cactus, Ardadslosttheplot, Nouvel Espoir and several others are natural hold-up horses, the compressed nature of a 5f field means many will be forced forward into positions that are not their preference. The bulk of the field carries REDISTRIBUTED tags precisely because there are far more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Nouvel Espoir, Cactus and Bold Optimist are the most likely to actually secure a mid-to-prominent position ahead of the majority. With a lone front-runner setting a controlled pace on good ground, the race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track Sovereign Cry and have something left for the final furlong, rather than genuine hold-up horses forced to cover ground they cannot recoup over five furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sovereign Cry Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Cry jumps cleanly and settles into an uncontested lead, controlling tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Sovereign Cry sets a measured pace on the stands rail and the race becomes a test of which prominently-placed horse can sustain their run through the final furlong; Jordan Breeze tracking closely is ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominents Flood The Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Jordan Breeze and several redistributed horses push forward early, creating a contested pace.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo over 5f on good ground compresses the field and stops the pace-setter, bringing hold-up horses marginally into the picture.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and a genuine hold-up horse finds a gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: On a flat 5f course in good ground this shape is feasible but constrained — with so many pseudo-closers actually racing mid-field, a true come-from-behind effort requires a fast pace that is not guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Cry sets a crawl and the race turns into a sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A bunch finish benefits those with the sharpest sectional speed off a slow pace; apprentice jockey handling and draw management become critical factors in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Sovereign Cry jumping cleanly from the gates is critical — if he misses the break, there is no horse in this field confirmed to step in as pace-setter and the entire race shape becomes chaotic.

White Smoke runs just one day after her previous start — monitor market moves and any pre-race reports from the Grassick yard, as a one-day turnaround on turf is unusual and could mean she is below her best.

Several apprentice jockeys (Wallace 7, Kennedy, Casey 7, Parsons 7, Frain 7, Browne-Souza 7, Tynan 7, Tormey 7) are riding hold-up horses pushed forward — inexperienced riders failing to settle their mounts could inflate the early pace beyond what Sovereign Cry intends.

Ardadslosttheplot returns after 277 days off for David Marnane; watch the betting for any significant market support that might indicate strong stable confidence despite the lengthy absence and step down in trip.
Jordan Breeze is the only non-front-running horse whose natural style (prominent) genuinely fits this race shape without redistribution — if she is nibbled at in the market it deserves attention.

runners_data.name: Florida Bay
runners_data.comment: Broke his maiden by a short margin at Fairyhouse last time, also placed third before that, and with course, distance and good ground proven for a yard that landed this contest last year, rates 99 and the one to beat up in grade.

runners_data.name: One Number
runners_data.comment: Found the company too strong down the field in a Listed race at Ascot last time, though the runner-up effort before that is more encouraging form. Well suited by this going, and with room for improvement now stepping up in trip again, he's yet to win in two starts but rates a workable 86 for this test.

runners_data.name: Wo Wo Never
runners_data.comment: A big impression on debut, third but beaten 11 lengths in a maiden at Gowran Park, points to more improvement with today's trip already proven. Regarded as having real physical scope, though this looks a tougher task, and he's yet to win, rated 90.

runners_data.name: Ranting Duke
runners_data.comment: Disqualified last time, but the placed effort before that reads well — second beaten just a length in a novice at York, finishing in a manner that suggested today's step up to a mile would suit even better. A stronger sort with more still to come, but the disqualification leaves a query, and he's rated bottom of the pack on today's figures at 84.

runners_data.name: Sarah's Choice
runners_data.comment: A daughter of Blue Point out of a dam who was herself useful at 6f as a two-year-old, this 100,000-euro breeze-up purchase is a half-sister to the useful Temple Of Hera and, foaled in February, should already have the scope for this level. She steps out without any recorded form, though, and the view is that debut success may be a stretch, so respect for the pedigree should be tempered by that first-time question mark.

runners_data.name: Tosca No Candis
runners_data.comment: Showed encouraging signs on her sole start, beaten 4 lengths in an auction race at Leopardstown, with today's trip and going already proven. She's yet to win, though, and with more needed to bridge the gap in this field, she's up against it on a rating of 84.

runners_data.name: Dancing Destiny
runners_data.comment: A below-form fourth at Fairyhouse last time, beaten 10 lengths, follows a third and a win before that, so there's more substance here than the latest line suggests. Up to a mile now, with course, distance and good ground all in her favour, she's a leading threat on 97.

runners_data.name: Cedrela
runners_data.comment: By Wooded and out of a family that includes a 7f winner in France, this 41,000-euro purchase — foaled in February — arrives with physical maturity and pedigree appeal, and the yard have a reputation for readying newcomers. It's a stiff race for a debutant, though, with this outing viewed more as an educational run than a serious tilt, on a rating of 93.

runners_data.name: Drowsy Maggie
runners_data.comment: Struggled on her only start, well beaten in a maiden at Ballinrobe, with a great deal of improvement needed to figure at this level. Unproven over today's trip, and rated bottom of the field on 48, she has plenty to prove against this field.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Gold
runners_data.comment: Struggled to see out the trip when down the field in an auction race at The Curragh last time, continuing a run of four starts without a win. Conditions have yet to click for her, and although today's distance has been covered before, plenty more improvement is needed on a rating of 54.

runners_data.name: Bofa Beach
runners_data.comment: A below-form run last time, failing to last home over 10f down the field in a maiden at Gowran Park, should find today's shorter trip much more to her liking, a distance she's already proven over. A third and a fourth also feature in four starts, and with course and going both suiting, she's one of the leading dangers on 76.

runners_data.name: Donna Time
runners_data.comment: Bred with stamina in mind, she matched recent expectations when beaten 8 lengths in an auction race at Leopardstown last time, having come back from a break, with a seventh the run before. Further progress looks more likely in handicaps down the line, and she's up against it on a rating of 60 today.

runners_data.name: Mai Dahlia
runners_data.comment: Market support followed her into a maiden at Fairyhouse last time, and she rewarded that faith with a second, beaten 6 lengths, backing up a third before that. Today's mile and good ground are both proven, and with room for more up in trip plus a first-time tongue-tie added, she's a leading contender on 76.

runners_data.name: Serendipia
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten eighth here last time, some way below her true level, came after a sixth on her only other start, and there's scope for a little natural progress now that early experience is banked. A tongue-tie is added for the first time, and having had only a short break since, she's a workmanlike 60 on today's figures.

runners_data.name: Sibaza
runners_data.comment: By Night Of Thunder and out of a useful mare who excelled at 7f, this newcomer is also a half-sister to the useful Simiyann, effective over twice the trip, giving her a broad spread of inherited ability. The stable have a solid record in this race, taking it twice in the last nine runnings, and although the view is that watching her debut may be wiser than backing it, she rates the one to beat on 77.

runners_data.name: Xirivella
runners_data.comment: A Gleneagles filly who cost 23,000 euros, there's a professional pedigree and price tag behind this newcomer suggesting physical promise. The concern is that today's race looks a stiff test for a first assignment, so she may need the experience before showing her true colours, rated 64.

races.name: Care At Home Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Chapel Island
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for A. Oliver who has shown a tendency to fade late in the finish; four of last five runs ended outside the placings and the step up to 1m3f looks a necessary requirement, but there is no evidence yet that the trip transforms the picture.
runners_data.comment: Held comfortably in a handicap at Down Royal last time, continuing a run of below-form efforts, but with course, distance and cut in the ground all proven and a first-time tongue-tie now added, there could be more to come off a mark of 60. A return to form is needed, but he tops our figures at 74 as the most likely.

runners_data.name: Connecteo
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead from a natural hold-up profile — a genuine caveat — but remains the sole likely pace-setter in this field; ran second over 12f on good ground in recent form, so the trip is not a concern, though racing out of role means its winning chance should be tempered.
runners_data.comment: Market confidence followed him into a handicap at Down Royal last time, and although beaten 8 1/2 lengths in fourth, that run has since been given a boost, with more progress expected. A second features among his last five starts, and with course, distance and going all proven, plus a first-time tongue-tie added, he's a fair each-way sort at 64 off a mark of 60.

runners_data.name: Rodeo Blues
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the mount for Joseph O'Brien, who has fired eight winners from 52 runners in the last 14 days; won over 10f on good ground in latest start and this 1m3f trip on a flat course looks tailor-made for a horse with a natural hold-up style and proven course-relevant form.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap readily at Ballinrobe last time, beating that field by 3 1/4 lengths, and the belief is there's more to come. That success, though, came from 12lb lower than today's mark, so she must defy a substantial rise, but on today's proven going she still rates one of the leading dangers on 72.

runners_data.name: The Holy Apostle
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Brendan Duke, whose trainer strike rate is modest; placed fifth over 1m3f on soft last time out, and the switch to good ground here brings a slight question mark given the form pattern on softer surfaces.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to see out the trip when down the field in a handicap at Down Royal last time, though he's already shown ability at 7f to a mile and should get further as he matures. A first-time hood is added today, and with a mark of 59 that looks full value already, he's up against it to improve much more, rated 65.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Noel Meade runner who fades late and has been outside the first six in all five recent starts, including on good ground; the 29-day break and a modest OR of 56 make it hard to make a case without a significant performance turnaround.
runners_data.comment: A blend of speed and stamina in the pedigree gives hope that today's step up in trip could suit, though his recent handicap form has been well beaten, most recently at Fairyhouse. Major improvement is still needed to justify a rating of 71 against a mark of 56, but he's included among the leading dangers on our figures.

runners_data.name: Point Cartwright
runners_data.note: Finished second over 12f on good ground most recently, which is a strong form line for this race; tends to fade in the finish, but the 1m3f trip at Naas on good going maps closely to that effort and the Adrian McGuinness yard has had two winners from 28 runners over the fortnight.
runners_data.comment: The trip suited well when beaten just 3 1/2 lengths at Limerick last time, off a mark 2lb lower than today's, and with further scope to go up again in distance, there's more to come. Course, distance and going are all proven, and he's rated 70 on our figures, though the yard's recent form is subdued, with just one winner from 27 runners in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Maker's Mark
runners_data.note: Genuine back-of-the-field type who has been shifted into a midfield slot given the density of hold-up horses; five runs without a win or place on good ground is a concern, and the apprentice claiming seven pounds is the main mitigating angle.
runners_data.comment: Raced too freely and faded late when stepped up in trip last time, comfortably held in a handicap at Down Royal, and with a sharper 7-8f seemingly more her game, today's even longer test looks a stretch further. Results have been mixed through a short career, leaving her towards the back of the pack on 55.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer placed into midfield by the race shape; has posted four placings in the last five runs, most on soft or good-to-soft, and the straight good ground at Naas could be a slight step up in terms of surface requirements, though the STYLE_FIT of 0.90 means the mapped position is not its natural berth.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form when beaten just 2 1/2 lengths off this same mark at Leopardstown last time, and with a string of fourths through his recent starts, he's a picture of consistency if unspectacular. Conditions today are already proven, and there's a fair chance again on a rating of 57 against a mark of 52.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: A horse who has been consistently placed in the bottom half of the field across six runs; Charles Weld is a trainer without recent runners in the data window, and the history in a hood (hg:p) has not unlocked any improvement — mapped to midfield but travels from further back.
runners_data.comment: The trip suited well when beaten 7 lengths in a handicap at Leopardstown last time, and she acts on cut ground, which should be relevant again. Further middle-distance targets look the long-term plan, and with cheekpieces fitted for the first time today, she's rated 56 against a mark of 51.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Returning from a 155-day absence and has raced exclusively on Polytrack; the switch to turf on good ground at Naas is a significant unknown and the long layoff adds risk — naturally runs from the rear and sits in midfield here only because of the crowded hold-up contingent.
runners_data.comment: Tracking the pace too keenly told when beaten 7 lengths in a handicap at Dundalk last time, and although the mark keeps easing, the overall form has faded, a concern after 155 days off. Effective at 7-8f and adaptable on turf and all-weather, with a tongue-tie fitted for the first time, she's rated 57 against a mark of 51.

runners_data.name: Six Wings
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has finished in the middle third of the field in all four career starts, all on good ground; Paul Flynn has had one winner from 13 runners over 14 days and the headgear combination (hg:tp) has not produced a notable forward move yet.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to find conditions to suit in a maiden at Limerick last time, well beaten, and results have been modest throughout a short career to date. Cheekpieces are fitted for the first time today, and with today's going already proven, she's rated 66 against a mark of 50, in the middle of this large field.

runners_data.name: Darwin's Angel
runners_data.note: Blinkers fitted (hg:v) for S.M. Duffy who has had one winner from four recent runners; 57 days between runs and a history of finishing sixth to thirteenth suggests the blinkers are an attempt to sharpen a horse that hasn't found a way to compete — true hold-up type in a midfield slot.
runners_data.comment: Out of sorts of late, well held in a claimer at Ballinrobe last time, but a first-time visor and a fresh break since could bring about a change of fortune. She stays 7f and handles good and all-weather ground, and although out of form recently, she rates a workable 69 against a modest mark of 47.

runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Has a third-place finish over 10f on good ground in the past which is arguably the most relevant positive piece of form here; apprentice Neve Bennett claiming seven pounds is useful but the horse's history of fading and lowest OR in the race (42) means it needs everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: The trip played to his strengths when third, beaten 7 lengths, in a handicap at Gowran Park last time. There's a speedy pedigree behind him best suited to 6f, though he still needs more to make an impact in handicap company, and he's rated low in the weights on 52 against a mark of 42.

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Placed fifth and sixth in 10f handicaps on good ground, with a reasonable line of form for this trip; Robyn Donaghue-Leahy claiming seven pounds adds weight, but the trainer Duke has no winners from four recent runners and the STYLE_FIT flag signals this is not a natural midfield horse.
runners_data.comment: A workmanlike sixth, 6 1/4 lengths back, in a handicap at Ballinrobe last time, and he's rated better over a shorter 7f, which is a query at today's longer trip. Heavy ground would bring out the best in him, and on a rating of 59 against a mark of 42, he's around the middle of this field.

runners_data.name: Jewels Legacy
runners_data.note: Has finished ninth in two of the last three starts and wears a hood (hg:b); OR of 41 is the joint-lowest in the race and the historical flat line across five runs on good ground suggests the redistribution out of a true hold-up role does not help.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to last home when beaten 8 lengths in a handicap at Leopardstown last time, and she's yet to show much of note through her career so far. First-time blinkers are added today, and with 7f her more effective trip, she's towards the foot of the field on a rating of 52 against a mark of 41.

runners_data.name: Swift Charm
runners_data.note: Two third-place finishes in 10f races on good ground in recent form gives Swift Charm a genuinely competitive form profile; W.R. Crawford's runner wears hood and tongue-tie (hg:ht) and the natural tendency to race hold-up is reflected in the STYLE_FIT flag — those good-ground thirds are the key angle.
runners_data.comment: Well held in a handicap at Down Royal last time, though a pair of thirds beforehand points to a better level, and there's a squeeze into contention if she can build on that last experience. Course, distance and going are all proven, and a first-time hood is added for a possible boost, rated 57 against a mark of 51.

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on good ground just one day ago, which is an immediately relevant performance on the card — the trainer McIntyre sends a horse with fresh winning form, and despite being tagged with a fade tendency and a hold-up style that places it in midfield here, the recency and distance match make it notable.
runners_data.comment: A dreadful start effectively ended his chance in a handicap at Leopardstown last time, beaten 6 1/4 lengths having missed the break completely, and there should be considerably more to come from him than that. Bred for 8-10f, with today's distance already covered, and a first-time hood added, he's rated 51 against a mark of 52, low among these on official figures.

runners_data.name: Music And Song
runners_data.note: No jockey recorded, which is itself a flag; OR of 40 and a history of finishing in the middle to rear of the field across multiple 10f runs limits the case significantly — placed in a hood (hg:p) and mapped to midfield from a natural rear position.
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard and could only manage fourth, beaten 10 lengths, in a claimer at Ballinrobe last time, and she's yet to show any real ability through her recent starts so far. First-time cheekpieces are added in an attempt to settle her better, and on a rating of 54 against a mark of 40, she's rated at the bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Flagstone Lady
runners_data.note: No jockey declared, which is an obvious concern for a 19-runner handicap; has not placed in four career starts and the OR of 53 sits mid-table but the absence of a rider confirmation at this stage is a practical negative regardless of the pace-shape implications.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to see out the trip down the field in a handicap at Ballinrobe last time, and today's step up in distance ought to suit her better as a result. Recent form has been modest overall, and on a rating of 55 against a mark of 53, she sits towards the lower end of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Connecteo is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, despite being a natural hold-up type redistributed to the lead, is the most likely pace-setter — meaning this race is set to be run at a controlled, uncontested tempo over 1m3f on good ground at Naas. With no genuine speed horse pressing from outside, the gallop is likely to be measured and sustainable rather than truly searching, which will compress the field and keep the leaders fresh into the straight. The field is packed with hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield because there are far more genuine come-from-behind horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Flagstone Lady, Private Larry, Nephin Mountain, Swift Charm and others are authentic hold-up performers who will be squeezed into the middle of the pack rather than their natural position. This controlled pace from a single front-runner favours horses with a prominent cruising speed or the ability to travel just off the pace and quicken when the tempo lifts — pure closers who need a truly strong gallop to produce their best are at a structural disadvantage here, as the steady pace is unlikely to string the field out sufficiently to create the gaps they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Connecteo Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Connecteo is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged and the field settles into a compact, processional gallop.
scenarios.body: Connecteo sets a comfortable rhythm and the race becomes a test of stamina and cruising speed rather than raw finishing pace, suiting horses who can track the leader and produce a sustained effort rather than a late burst; the trip and good ground reward horses with a clean jumping-off point from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positioned just off Connecteo's shoulder travels strongly and seizes the advantage two furlongs out before the hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: The controlled tempo means the horse in second or third position expends little energy in the middle stages and has enough petrol left to kick decisively when the race begins in earnest; this scenario rewards any runner able to secure a prominent position early in the large 19-runner field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Benefit from Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong in the final half-mile and the prominent horses empty, leaving the door open for genuine hold-up types to sweep through.
scenarios.body: In this shape, horses who have been conserved at the back of the midfield group get a clear run as the race opens up, but the structural reality is that most of the nominal hold-up types here have been pushed out of their natural position and may not be tracking from far back enough to fully capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Creates Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If the large field bunches and there is interference or a significant change of pace mid-race that scrambles running positions.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over 1m3f the early stages could become congested and positional shuffling may benefit a horse that breaks cleanly and avoids trouble, while turning what should be an orderly race into a tactical lottery; this scenario is the least likely given the single-pace-setter dynamic.

watchPoints.text: Private Larry won over 12f on good ground just one day ago — connections have clearly targeted this race fast and if the horse recovers quickly, the recency of that winning effort at the right trip is the single most dangerous form line in the race.

Rodeo Blues represents the live combination of Dylan Browne McMonagle and a red-hot Joseph O'Brien yard (8 wins from 52 in 14 days) and the horse won over 10f on good ground last time — watch for it to be placed prominently just off Connecteo.

With 19 runners at the 1m3f start, the opening half-furlong is likely to be congested — any horse drawn wide or slow to break could find itself trapped in traffic before the field settles, with Swift Charm and Six Wings the most vulnerable given their true hold-up styles being pushed into unnatural midfield positions.

Connecteo is racing entirely out of natural style at the head of affairs — if it fails to travel comfortably in front or is bustled along early, the lack of a genuine replacement pace-setter means the race could go false very quickly in the final three furlongs.

Flagstone Lady and Music And Song both have no jockey recorded — monitor declarations closely as late withdrawals from a 19-runner field will affect the pace map, particularly if any confirmed prominent types are removed.

races.name: TRM Stay Cool Stay Sound Rated Race

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with strong good-ground form (5 from 5 in similar conditions) and two wins at 6f before being stepped up to 7f; OR 98 at top of the weights but 83 days off the track for G M Lyons, whose 14-day strike rate of 2/20 tempers confidence, and racing out of her natural lead role somewhat given the gap in class here.
runners_data.comment: Failed to settle down the field in a Group 3 at Leopardstown last time, a disappointing return that raises a slight question mark, but a pair of wins earlier in that sequence showed she's clearly up to this level. Course, distance and good ground are all proven, a first-time tongue-tie is added to help her relax, and with the trainer in good form, she's a leading danger on 91 despite that below-par latest run.

runners_data.name: Yaupon De Replay
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for Joseph O'Brien's lightly-raced three-year-old who won over 6f on good ground and placed at 7f on soft — the step back to good turf is a mild positive but limited form (3 career runs, one on good at 7f) means this is still an unknown quantity despite the top jockey booking.
runners_data.comment: Down the field in a Group 3 at Chantilly last time, well below the level shown when winning two starts back, and this stable has a good record in this event, having taken it last year. Course and distance form is there, but 81 days since her latest outing and only a moderate recent level leave her the outsider of this six on a rating of 86.

runners_data.name: Frescobaldi
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this Daniel Murphy-trained runner who has genuine 7f form on good turf (a win and two placed efforts in similar conditions from 7 comparable runs), and his style as a natural prominent type gives him every chance to track Suzie Songs and produce a clean run through; the trainer's 0/4 recent 14-day strike rate is the only mild flag.
runners_data.comment: Below-par down the field in a Listed race at Newbury last time, tried in cheekpieces without success, but that followed a good run of form beforehand, and a drop back in grade today should suit. Course, distance and good ground are all proven, and he's rated a leading danger on 89.

runners_data.name: Ocean's Breath
runners_data.note: Most recent winner over this exact 7f trip on good turf for G M Lyons, which is compelling form, and Gary Carroll aboard is a strong positive; this horse wants to race prominently and is most likely among the redistributed runners to actually secure that position close to Suzie Songs, making the style-fit discount less damaging than for the others pushed back on the map.
runners_data.comment: Stepped up in trip to win a 3yo race at Fairyhouse by 3 lengths last time, backing up a progressive profile that suggests there's more to come back in handicap company. Course, distance and good ground are all proven, a first-time tongue-tie is added, and with the yard in excellent recent form, he heads our figures at 91 as the horse to beat.

runners_data.name: L L Koulsty
runners_data.note: Rory Mulligan (5lb claimer) partners this John O'Donoghue-trained runner who won at 7f on Heavy at Haydock and most recently scored over 6f on Soft — the switch to good ground at Naas is a concern given 0 wins or places from 6 runs on comparable going; naturally a front-running type crowded out of position here, which compounds the going question.
runners_data.comment: A drop in trip suited when landing a handicap at Cork by 1 1/2 lengths last time, continuing a steady upward curve through his last five starts. Course, distance and good ground are all proven, and he's rated a leading danger on 90.

runners_data.name: Sir Benji
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's runner has only two career starts — a win over 10f on Heavy and a third over 10f on Good — making the drop to 7f on good turf a significant unknown; a genuine prominent-style horse who cannot get his natural position in this shape, and with so little form to assess, Robert Whearty faces a difficult task working out where to slot him early.
runners_data.comment: Backed up a winning debut by matching that level when third in an auction race at Roscommon last time, and he's clearly held in high regard as a smart prospect. Today's step down in trip is the obvious question given he looks better served by galloping on further, with 10f his proven trip on easy or good going, leaving him respected but with a slight query on 88.

races.paceDynamic: Suzie Songs is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push her early, she is likely to control this 7f contest at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on good ground at Naas. The pace she sets will be honest rather than searingly fast, creating a race where runners can track her without burning excessive energy — a shape that traditionally favours those able to sit just off the leader and pounce in the straight. Frescobaldi and Yaupon De Replay are best placed to exploit that tempo from prominent-to-midfield positions, while Ocean's Breath, L L Koulsty, and Sir Benji are genuine prominent types who have been pushed back on the map because Suzie Songs occupies the lead and there is simply no room for all of them to race where they naturally want to — whichever of that trio best manoeuvres to sit second or third early will be best served; Ocean's Breath, given recent course winning form, is most likely to secure that slot. This race shape — a lone uncontested front-runner dictating a measured pace — strongly favours races-prominently types who can travel close to the fractions and produce a sustained run through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Suzie Songs Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Suzie Songs leads without interference and sets a measured, uncontested pace throughout the 7f
scenarios.body: Suzie Songs dictates from the front at her own rhythm on ground she acts on (5/5 in similar going), and a horse that can track her through the bend and accelerate in the straight benefits from the controlled fractions; the sustained 7f tempo on good turf rewards prominent runners with a genuine finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracking Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to soften Suzie Songs and a hold-up or midfield runner picks up the pieces
scenarios.body: Yaupon De Replay, trained by Joseph O'Brien and ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle, is the natural candidate to swoop from off the pace if the fractions prove quicker than expected for this field; Frescobaldi's positional versatility also allows it to drop slightly deeper and finish powerfully if the race tempo elevates.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crowded Prominent Brawl Erupts
scenarios.trigger: If Ocean's Breath, L L Koulsty, and Sir Benji all push forward aggressively to claim the position they naturally want, forcing a contested pace
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated tempo would burn off front-end horses and open the race for runners who can settle slightly further back and finish on the bridle; Yaupon De Replay and Frescobaldi would be the chief beneficiaries of a pace collapse triggered by multiple prominent types fighting for position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the scramble for position causes erratic fractions and an unfancied prominent runner finds an uncontested slot
scenarios.body: L L Koulsty, a winner over this 7f trip at Haydock and most recently at 6f, could steal an uncontested rail run if the prominent pack creates gaps; Sir Benji, still learning after just two career starts, remains a wildcard if the race fragments into multiple fractions.

watchPoints.text: Ocean's Breath and L L Koulsty are both natural prominent types likely to push forward from the gates — watch the first two furlongs for a positional battle that could compress the pace or cause interference near Suzie Songs.

Suzie Songs has been off the track for 83 days and is top weight at OR 98 — if she is fractionally short of peak fitness the controlled pace she typically sets could evaporate in the closing stages, collapsing the dominant scenario.

L L Koulsty has zero wins or places from 6 runs on comparable good ground despite winning on heavy and soft — the going is a genuine concern and punters should note the style displacement compounds rather than softens that risk.

Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking for Yaupon De Replay is noteworthy for a horse with only three career runs — O'Brien does not typically engage this jockey without expectation, and the hold-up profile could be well-suited if the pace scenario elevates slightly above its projected controlled tempo.
